SUPERVISOR — diagnostic refinement from the user on the jitter, verbatim: "what doesnt make much sense to me either way about the lag is that my camera is like butter. my movement feels like a rubberband". Camera smooth + player rubberbanding is a POSITION-CORRECTION signature, not frame-time: the rendered player is being pulled between two disagreeing position sources. Your frame table (still owed from the original dispatch) must now log per render frame: input intent, rendered model position, latest physics-step position, and any correction/snap events. Three specific suspects to check IN THE DATA: (1) any smoothing/interpolation layer on the player position — including whatever remains of your slomo attempt — lagging behind input then catching up IS the rubberband; (2) the repeated heightfield.register events visible in the user's dev log firing mid-play — each re-registration can re-resolve ground and yank the pose (why are they re-firing at all during normal play?); (3) the physics step rate vs render rate without proper interpolation. The UI-flap CONTENT SWAP work remains real but separate — the rubberband is the position pipeline. Same done-bar: frame table first, named cause, fix shape proposed to supervisor before building.
SUPERVISOR — another missing port for your queue, and it JUMPS AHEAD of PERFLOG2 because it unblocks the user's own rubberband triage. NOCLIP-0606, user verbatim: "hm. they never ported noclip command either. which is dumb so i cant say if its movement or not because i can only move normally also". Port the noclip console command faithfully from the reference implementation (love2d tree / the original console verbs source — copy its exact behavior and toggle semantics, do not invent). Noclip matters diagnostically RIGHT NOW: with it, the user can fly without physics — if movement is smooth in noclip the rubberband lives in the physics/correction pipeline, if it still rubberbands the problem is in the render/position path. That is also data for YOUR hunt — when it lands, note the implication in your frame-table analysis. DONE-BAR: noclip works in the live console with reference semantics + verify green + READY. DO NOT COMMIT. User confirmation is the PASS.
SUPERVISOR — idle-session data for your UIFLAP/rubberband hunt: with the user SITTING IDLE, spikewatch fires on a ~95-100 frame (~0.4s) rhythm with THREE signatures: (1) your known CONTENT SWAP flap (~11 nodes / 78 glyphs A/B toggle, frame_hash alternating between the same values); (2) REPAINT with NO tree change — "inline-prop / animated-value churn", glyph_count 239->285 (+46) repeating, meaning some text/value re-renders and re-uploads the full 2D buffer every beat; (3) GC/NATIVE spikes that correlate with repeated heightfield re-registration (another lane is gating that). All three share ONE ~0.4s heartbeat. Find the timer: something ticks every ~0.4s and drives a text/value update that mounts/unmounts a ~11-node subtree AND churns an animated/inline value. Correlate the beat period with every interval/timer/poll in the play stack. Console remains eliminated. Same done-bar: name the component/timer with file:line evidence.
resolution: Resolved in b91a941962eeb56e3cbc631f1ac39f2ce59f10d7. Added the render-frame movement witness, noclip split support, heightfield registration ownership/gating, live-floor recovery checks, and floor-edge side-push grace so the player is not visually pulled between disagreeing position sources. The user confirmed walking is no longer choppy.
